title: viscum laxum subsp. austriacum
intro: Viscum laxum subsp. austriacum, commonly known as European mistletoe, is a parasitic plant that grows on the branches of various tree species, particularly oak and apple trees. European mistletoe has been used in traditional medicine to promote health and well-being, with benefits including relief from stress, anxiety, and insomnia, as well as boosting the immune system. The therapeutic actions of European mistletoe include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory effects, which contribute to its potential in cancer treatment and prevention. The bioactive constituents of European mistletoe include viscotoxins, alkaloids, and polysaccharides, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and are being studied for their potential in various medical applications.
